question: What is the primary purpose of a Drug Revolving Fund in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To generate heavy profits for hospital expansion projects
options.B: To provide completely free healthcare services to all citizens
options.C: To guarantee a steady and reliable supply of essential medicines
options.D: To manage staff salaries and administrative overhead costs

explanation: The DRF mechanism is specifically structured to eliminate drug stockouts by using revenue from sales exclusively for continuous restocking. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: How does the initial seed capital of a DRF function once the scheme is running?

options.A: It is locked in a bank account to earn fixed interest
options.B: It continuously converts between cash and pharmaceutical inventory
options.C: It is distributed among senior hospital management as bonuses
options.D: It is paid back to the government in annual installments

explanation: Seed capital provides the first batch of drugs; when sold, the cash is used to buy more stock, creating a perpetual revolving cycle. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which principle ensures that DRF drugs are priced reasonably for everyday patients?
explanation: The affordability principle balances fair pricing so that low-income patients can access necessary treatments without financial ruin. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why is financial self-sustainability considered a critical core principle of the DRF?

options.A: It allows the hospital to stop charging patients for services entirely
options.B: It ensures the fund can continuously restock without relying on constant government bailouts
options.C: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies will provide free donations
options.D: It eliminates the need for any professional auditing or bookkeeping

explanation: Self-sustainability protects the scheme from collapsing when government subventions are delayed or unavailable. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the DRF Management Committee?

options.A: To manufacture essential generic drugs locally within the hospital ward
options.B: To handle the personal nursing care plans of surgical patients
options.C: To oversee pricing policies, review stock reports, and prevent financial leakages
options.D: To personally prescribe medications to every admitted patient

explanation: A committee provides multi-sectoral oversight, ensuring financial integrity and steady operational management. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is separation of duties enforced in the day-to-day operation of a DRF?

options.A: To reduce the total number of working hours for hospital staff
options.B: To make the procurement process slower and more deliberate
options.C: To prevent pilferage and unauthorized handling of cash and drug inventory
options.D: To ensure that nurses never have to touch a prescription pad

explanation: Separating cash handlers from inventory managers introduces internal checks that significantly lower the risk of fraud and stock discrepancies. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: What inventory control rule dictates that products with the nearest expiry dates must be issued out first?
explanation: The FEFO principle directly minimizes financial loss caused by pharmaceutical stock expiring on hospital shelves. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is procurement restricted to an Essential Medicines List (EML) within a DRF?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any storage facilities in the hospital
options.B: To ensure that pharmaceutical companies give the hospital free samples
options.C: To prevent capital from being tied up in rarely used or non-essential drugs
options.D: To make doctors prescribe only herbal remedies to patients

explanation: Restricting purchases to the EML guarantees that limited funds are spent exclusively on high-demand, life-saving medicines that turn over quickly. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the purpose of adding a markup percentage to the procurement cost of DRF drugs?

options.A: To cover inflation, logistics, and replace sold stock effectively
options.B: To fund luxury international travels for hospital management
options.C: To pay the personal income taxes of all clinical nurses
options.D: To discourage patients from purchasing prescribed medications

explanation: A calculated markup absorbs operational overhead and inflationary pressures so the capital base retains its purchasing power. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which practice poses the greatest immediate threat to the cash flow of a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Purchasing high-turnover essential medicines in bulk
options.B: Uncontrolled credit sales and unrecovered debt waivers
options.C: Strict adherence to the First-Expire, First-Out storage rule
options.D: Conducting routine internal financial audits of pharmacy ledgers

explanation: Giving out drugs on credit without repayment drains liquid cash, making it impossible for the pharmacy to restock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h5)

question: How do nurses directly contribute to the success of the Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: By setting the wholesale procurement prices for pharmaceutical companies
options.B: By auditing the central bank accounts of the hospital management
options.C: By manufacturing generic intravenous fluids in the hospital ward
options.D: By promoting patient adherence and reporting near-expiry ward stock

explanation: Nurses protect the fund by ensuring drugs are used properly by patients and identifying wasted or expiring inventory at the ward level. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the clinical significance of nurses reporting sudden surges in medication demand to the pharmacy unit?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any financial auditing in the institution
options.B: It helps the pharmacy adjust quantification data to prevent unexpected stockouts
options.C: It allows the hospital to increase the profit markup on those specific drugs
options.D: It proves that the doctors are prescribing too many medications

explanation: Frontline clinical feedback alerts inventory managers to epidemiological shifts, ensuring accurate forecasting and continuous drug availability. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which macroeconomic factor most rapidly erodes the purchasing power of a revolving fund?

options.C: Strict adherence to essential medicines lists

explanation: When prices surge rapidly, cash collected from drug sales loses its value and cannot purchase equivalent stock quantities. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the consequence when hospital management diverts DRF capital to pay utility bills or buy generator fuel?

options.A: It forces pharmaceutical companies to offer permanent price discounts
options.B: It improves the accuracy of the hospital inventory quantification
options.C: It breaks the revolving cycle and leads directly to severe drug stockouts
options.D: It strengthens the financial sustainability of the pharmacy department

explanation: DRF capital is ring-fenced for drug procurement; diverting it for general hospital overhead depletes inventory and halts the revolving mechanism. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is considered a key performance indicator for evaluating a DRF?

options.A: Frequency of international travel by the hospital board
options.B: Total number of private pharmacies built in the local community
options.C: Inventory turnover rate and capital recovery rate
options.D: Amount of free medical advice given by administrative staff

explanation: Turnover and recovery rates measure how efficiently capital and drug stock are circulating within the system. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why are periodic price reviews necessary for a sustainable Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: To ensure that all drugs are sold at a complete loss to the facility
options.B: To adjust markups realistically against inflation and maintain purchasing power
options.C: To eliminate the need for any internal or external auditing
options.D: To maximize hospital profits at the expense of vulnerable patients

explanation: Periodic reviews ensure pricing keeps pace with economic realities so the fund can continuously replace sold inventory. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h8)
